clue.text: Don't tell anyone I demolish unfinished wine

parts.note: SH is the hushing call that asks someone to keep a secret

indicators.note: unfinished says the synonym for demolish loses its final letter

parts.note: to raze a building is to demolish it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses in a whisper to smashing a half-drunk bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiraz is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, so it is a type of wine.

clue.text: American vessel south of landing point getting fish

parts.note: a helipad is marked with a big H where the helicopter lands
USS (United States Ship) is the prefix of an American navy vessel

explanation.surface: A US ship docks at a jetty and takes on a catch of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' is an indicator on the charade: in a down clue the vessel sits below the landing point.
explanation.definitionFit: Huss is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish and related small sharks sold as food.

clue.text: Hybrid cattle run backward

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Crossbred cows stampede in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition, as in 'backward in coming forward'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone backward in coming forward is shy and unwilling, so backward here means hesitant or unwilling.

clue.text: Unknown replacing head on Disney film primarily about African nation

indicators.note: replacing head on says the first letter of the film title is swapped for the unknown

parts.note: Bambi is the Disney film about a young deer
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so Z is an unknown

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A puzzle about swapping the opening of a Disney cartoon title, reading like a film-trivia question about Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa, formerly Northern Rhodesia.

clue.text: To co-operate intercepting wallaby, alpacas going west

indicators.note: going west says the hidden letters are read backwards
intercepting says the answer is caught in among the letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone working together with others to head off a wallaby and some alpacas as they run west.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'intercepting' in the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, catching letters inside 'wallaby, alpacas', and the definition is just 'To co-operate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work along with someone, so it means to co-operate.

clue.text: Money, crisps and book found by this nosy creature rifling around

indicators.note: rifling around is rummaging through, so the letters of money, crisps and book are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A curious animal rummages through someone's bag, finding cash, snacks and a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this nosy creature' has a pun: the animal is literally nosy, with a huge nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The proboscis monkey of Borneo is famous for the male's enormous drooping nose, making it a literally nosy animal.

clue.text: Getting on, carrying on in unison

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: getting on in years means ageing
RE means on, as in 'on the subject of'

explanation.surface: Elderly folk keep going together in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: People acting in unison are in full accord, of one mind on the matter, and so are concurring.

clue.text: Brick up a plant

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a slab is a flat block, like a brick

explanation.surface: An instruction to wall up a plant behind bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree known for its very light wood, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Gents, maybe, cut up when brought in to view new TV show

parts.note: the gents is a men's public toilet, an example of a loo

indicators.note: brought in to says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to see something is to view it

indicators.note: in a down answer, up says the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to mow grass is to cut it

explanation.surface: Men, perhaps, upset at being dragged along to watch a fresh television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose Women is a long-running British daytime TV talk show with an all-female panel, a joke against 'Gents'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose Women is an ITV lunchtime chat programme in Britain, so it is a TV show.

clue.text: Lime's cooked with duck three times — Neapolitan composition

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O; three times gives three of them

explanation.surface: A recipe: duck cooked with lime, repeated three times, framed as an Italian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: 'O sole mio' is a famous Neapolitan song of 1898, so it is a composition from Naples.

clue.text: I can't wait for chocolate containing large mango at centre

indicators.note: containing says the chocolate holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Rolo is a brand of chewy caramel-filled chocolates
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: at centre picks the middle letter of the word mango

explanation.surface: An impatient person longing for a chocolate with a mango filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'roll on Friday' expresses eager impatience for something to arrive, the same feeling as 'I can't wait for'.

clue.text: Helped around home — started with brass

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to help out on a joint task is to have co-operated
IN means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone helped out around the house, starting off with polishing the brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is British slang for money, here coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated machine is set going by money, and brass is old British slang for money.

clue.text: Agitated EU warn island that's turned — it's not good to assume

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so these letters are stirred into a new order
turned says the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: A worried European Union warns an island with a sudden change of heart against making presumptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' means to put on clothes, not to presume.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a garment is to put it on, so something not good to put on is unfit to be worn.

clue.text: Animated princess polished off starter of divine food

indicators.note: polished off starter of says the first letter is removed

parts.note: manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites in the wilderness

explanation.surface: A cartoon royal finishes off a heavenly first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polished off' reads as eating, but it means taking away the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is one of the two royal sisters in Disney's cartoon film Frozen, an animated princess.

clue.text: No cost in going round lakeside location

indicators.note: going round suggests turning things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A free trip round a lake, framed as a travel tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Coniston is a village beside Coniston Water in England's Lake District, so it is a lakeside place.

clue.text: They'd help in fast races at sea

definitions.text: They'd help in fast races at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of fast races are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailing skills that would help win quick yacht races.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and 'at sea' does double duty as part of the picture and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seacraft is the skill of sailing and navigating, which would help anyone in a quick race on the water.

clue.text: Artist lifting mould and gripping cast at first

indicators.note: lifting, in a down answer, says the whole assembly is read from the bottom up

parts.note: mould is a kind of decay or rot

indicators.note: gripping says the word for and holds the next letter inside

parts.note: plus means and, as in two plus two

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word cast

explanation.surface: An artist raises a mould, holding the cast at the start of the process.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all bronze-casting terms, but 'mould' is decay and 'cast' supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor is an artist who makes three-dimensional work by carving or modelling.

clue.text: Summits mostly secretive in arrangement

indicators.note: in arrangement says the remaining letters are put in a new order
mostly says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Summit meetings, kept largely secret, being arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of 'secretive', and 'in arrangement' shuffles SECRETIV.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertex is the top or highest point of something, so the plural form is another word for peaks.

clue.text: Regularly sacrificing pieces, as chess masters

indicators.note: regularly sacrificing pieces says every other letter is given up, keeping the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Grandmasters who keep giving up pieces in their chess games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificing pieces' sounds like a chess gambit; here it means losing alternate letters of 'as chess'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert or star performer at something, so masters are experts of the same kind.

clue.text: Country having unlimited sugar and bananas

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, so the first and last letters are dropped
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of and are scrambled

explanation.surface: A country rich in sugar and bananas, both big African crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an East African country, a republic bordering Lake Victoria.

clue.text: Gang member dealt drug for criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A gang member peddled narcotics for a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' is the anagram signal, not part of the picture's crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is the pickpocket in Fagin's gang of boy thieves in Dickens's Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Quick learner divides imperial units

indicators.note: divides says the letter splits the other word by going inside it

parts.note: feet are units of length in the imperial system
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A bright student splits up imperial measurements quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet is a literary adjective meaning swift, as in fleet of foot.

clue.text: Type of cheese that's fruity

definitions.meaning: a veined cheese such as Stilton or Roquefort
fruity can mean risqué or suggestive, as in a smutty joke

explanation.surface: A cheese with fruity notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue cheese has mould veins; blue jokes are smutty, and fruity means similarly suggestive in British usage.

clue.text: A thing that doesn't start is woeful

indicators.note: that doesn't start says the first letter of the synonym is missing

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A broken gadget that won't start up is a sorry thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject means wretched or miserable, as in abject poverty, close to woeful.

clue.text: 1000 soldiers in one eastern county ousted by southern clan

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ousted by says the soldiers' letters are pushed out and replaced

parts.note: Norfolk is a county on England's east coast
OR means other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A thousand troops stationed in East Anglia are driven out by a family group from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' only links: the soldiers are those found in the county's name. Norfolk is an English county on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of related families, so it means one's relatives or extended family.

clue.text: Weapon theoretically destroyed Earth within 24 hours

indicators.note: within says the shuffled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of earth are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sci-fi weapon that could theoretically wipe out the planet in a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: A death ray is a beam weapon of science fiction, long proposed in theory but never really built.

clue.text: Oz state overwhelmed by a Royal Family member's return

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the state's letters are swallowed up between the others

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
NSW is New South Wales, a state of Australia (Oz)

explanation.surface: An Australian state outdone by a royal coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition, a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A return can be a reply, as in a quick return in conversation, so it means a response.
